title: Recapitulation of pathophysiological features of AD in SARS-CoV-2-infected subjects

genuine.note: 'As described previously (Burks et al., 2021)' for the HALO image-analysis method, but the reference is a review on routes of SARS-CoV-2 into the CNS with no methods section; the method is not described there.

false_alarm.note: The review documents SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis in the respiratory tract in depth, the 'well studied' part; that much less is known about neurological consequences is the citing authors' framing of the field.
Eu et al. discuss NGF supporting neuron survival and the NGF hypothesis of Alzheimer's disease, which is what the sentence says.

The review describes the NLRP3 inflammasome, caspase-1, IL-1β/IL-18 and gasdermin D pyroptosis cascade the citation is attached to; the TREM1 and SARS-CoV-2 link is the citing authors' hypothesis ('may impact').

debatable.note: The review supports IL-8's role in attracting neutrophils but does not mention endothelial cell migration; a partly supported list.

Only the abstract was available: Brison et al. show glutamate excitotoxicity drives paralysis and neuronal loss in mice infected with an HCoV-OC43 mutant; the cytokine mechanism is not in the abstract and may come from the co-cited Jacomy et al.

The review describes leukocyte infiltration and neuroinflammation with SARS-CoV-2 in the CNS; the general mechanism (peripheral cytokines recruiting leukocytes across the BBB) is textbook knowledge not stated in these terms in the review.

Hedged speculation ('it is possible ... may'): Meinhardt et al. show olfactory CNS entry and neuroinflammation, the premise, but say nothing about cognitive decline or AD; the co-cited Mhatre et al. (2015) predates SARS-CoV-2.

summary_line: Caught 7 of 8 planted errors · 3 false alarms · 1 real citation problem found in the original paper

details.description: Added the scope "in every population and setting" before the citation

Replaced the citation (Kovacs and Gelpi, 2012) with (Lampart et al., 2022) ("Clinical utility of inflammatory biomarkers in COVID-19 in direct comparison to other respiratory infections—A prospective cohort study") (similarity 0.27 vs 0.57 for the original)
Added the scope "universally, in all cases" before the citation

Replaced the citation (Tröscher et al., 2019; Fischer-Smith, 2001) with (Varet et al., 2016) ("SARTools: A DESeq2- and EdgeR-Based R Pipeline for Comprehensive Differential Analysis of RNA-Seq Data") (similarity 0.14 vs 0.65 for the original)
Added the scope "in every population and setting" before the citation
Replaced the citation (Serrano et al., 2021) with (Krämer et al., 2014) ("Causal analysis approaches in Ingenuity Pathway Analysis") (similarity 0.22 vs 0.73 for the original)

Replaced the citation (QIAGEN Inc, version 73620684; Krämer et al., 2014) with (Sullivan and Fischer, 2021) ("Age-Associated Neurological Complications of COVID-19: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis") (similarity 0.19 vs 0.71 for the original)
